tamkârum agents at the rate of 15 shekels (of silver)
each. Your tamkârum agents are reliable: you have nothing to fear. They are like us or you.
9-18We will send a hundred (cloth)-kutanum
and 4 donkeys with S1i-Bélum to Wahsušana for purchases, and
we will send Iddin-Adad with S1i-Bélum. On your evening, he will receive in money the price of your hundred fabrics that Sû-Bélum brings to Wahšušana. 19-27 As for the rest of your fabrics, we will deposit them for a period of 20 weeks in the charge of trusted agents for whom you will not have to worry about your money. In addition, we will enter the amount of money we have deposited with the tamkârum-agents as well as the names of your tamkârum-agents, and then our precise report will reach you.
28-34The orders of the karum are strict, therefore
for your smuggled (goods) about which you wrote to us, the time is not appropriate, and that
why Also we will not write to you about your smuggled goods. As for you, it is as

watch them carefully.

terms: “(Allow) that I leave in order to clear my property-
bûlâtuma and to lay before them (the donors) everything that there is. » Sil-Hubur offered me a term of 5 years, and you agreed. But I didn't agree, saying: "I don't want to wait 5 years!" I will complete the term that I asked of the god and I will release my bûlâtum property. »
I6-26Two or three of my tamkârum agents on whom I depend have no common sense. A large quantity of money escaped my hands. It is (however) not appropriate to reveal their names to you! Thus (speak) Aššur-idi: tell Aššur-nâdâ, lli-âLUM and
Aššur-taklâku.
5—11-How is it that your brother has been ill for 2 years, and you continue to trust him? Please, as soon as you read (this) letter, write so that he comes.

ogets, let him seal it and send it to me. Send me Aššur-

6.1.6. Iddin-Istar, the grandson
Iddin-Ištar, son of Aššur-nâdâ, after leaving his grandfather's house in Aššur, hardly has any contact with him anymore. Aššur-idi accuses his grandson of having fraudulently entered his house to steal the equivalent of 3 silver mines (131). Iddin-Ištar then settles in Durhumit where his father visits him (271). He sells the latter's goods and invests the capital in the copper trade (270); for this he goes to Burušhattum and Wahšušana when the political situation allows him (64). Iddin-Ištar defends his father's interests and property against his uncle lli-âLUM with whom he is in contact. In any case, his copper transactions are not always very successful (271)!

7.5.5. Lamassâtum
Lamassatum lives in Aššur, where she receives money
in the company of other women (VS 26, 162) and maintains
a correspondence with Pušu-kén. However, her letters
show that she owns a house in Kaniš where archives are stored. We can imagine that she was married to a merchant who died in Kaniš after having lived there for a few years, and that Lamassatum is seeking to regain possession of the latter's property there. It also maintains a commercial relationship with Sat-Ea (AKT 1, 1
et KTH 23 = EL 180).
